families.page_title: What to do in a radiation emergency
evidence_points: Radiation emergencies may involve nuclear facilities or transport of radioactive material.
Radioactive material may be released as gases, dust or larger fragments.

Going inside and staying inside can reduce exposure in many scenarios.
People should follow official information on sheltering, evacuation and other protective actions.
Government, local authorities and nuclear operators maintain emergency plans.

families.topic: removing radioactive material from skin, clothes and shoes and safely assisting others
families.page_title: How to remove radioactive material from your skin and clothes – self-decontamination guidance
evidence_points: The first priority near a radiation emergency is to go inside and stay inside.
People should close doors and windows and follow official updates.
Outer clothing and shoes should be removed carefully.
Removing outer clothing can remove a large proportion of deposited radioactive material.
Removed clothing should be sealed and kept away from people.
After washing, clean clothes should be put on and assistance to others should avoid spreading contamination.
